title: QUIC RFC 9000 0-RTT Remembered Transport Parameter Policy
purpose: Describe the bounded client-side policy for remembering only 0-RTT-eligible transport parameters from a detached resumption ticket carrier.
design_summary: The client-side resumption carrier now separates the raw peer transport-parameter snapshot from the subset that can be used to decide whether a dormant 0-RTT attempt has usable remembered transport parameters. QuicZeroRttTransportParameterPolicy defines the known transport-parameter identifiers and classifies each modeled parameter as mandatory, optional, or prohibited for 0-RTT storage. It builds a sanitized QuicTransportParameters snapshot containing only the processable parameters the runtime may remember for client 0-RTT, while leaving prohibited parameters such as max_ack_delay, preferred_address, stateless_reset_token, initial_source_connection_id, retry_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, and ack_delay_exponent out of the 0-RTT subset.
data_and_state_considerations: QuicDetachedResumptionTicketSnapshot continues to preserve the raw peer transport-parameter snapshot for resumption metadata and existing diagnostics. The new internal ZeroRttTransportParameters snapshot is derived once at ticket construction time and gates HasEarlyDataPrerequisiteMaterial, so a ticket containing only prohibited remembered values does not make the runtime report 0-RTT readiness.
edge_cases_and_constraints: ack_delay_exponent is classified as prohibited even though the current QuicTransportParameters model does not carry a dedicated field for it.
disable_active_migration is only treated as present in the remembered subset when it is true because the current model represents absence and false with the same boolean default.
A raw peer snapshot with only prohibited values is retained as metadata but does not enable dormant 0-RTT readiness.
No public early-data API, TLS early_data extension, server 0-RTT admission decision, or anti-replay policy is introduced by this slice.
risks: Future transport parameters must be added to the classification table before they can be safely remembered for 0-RTT.
The optional disable_active_migration parameter cannot distinguish explicit false from absence with the current runtime model.
This slice does not yet compare remembered values against server-side 0-RTT acceptance policy or enforce updated-value violations in 0-RTT packets.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the client remembered-transport-parameter policy floor for REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S7P4P1-0001, REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S7P4P1-0002, and REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-0346 only. The remaining S7P4P1 server acceptance, restored-value support, and updated-value violation requirements remain separate follow-on work.
